subject: general
question: Face cream belongs to which type of colloid form?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Emulsion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Face cream is an example of an emulsion**, which is a type of colloid where both the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium are liquids.
 
• An emulsion is formed when two immiscible liquids are mixed together, typically oil and water, with one being dispersed in the form of tiny droplets throughout the other.
 
• In face creams, the oil phase is usually dispersed within the water phase, creating an oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion.
 
• Emulsifiers are added to face creams to stabilize the emulsion, preventing the oil and water from separating.
 
• Common ingredients in face creams that act as emulsifiers include cetyl alcohol, stearic acid, and polysorbates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Emulsions**

 
 
• **Oil-in-Water (O/W) Emulsion:** Oil droplets are dispersed in water, commonly used in cosmetic creams and lotions.
 
• **Water-in-Oil (W/O) Emulsion:** Water droplets are dispersed in oil, typically used in heavy creams and ointments.
 
 
 
• **Emulsifiers**
 
 
• Emulsifiers are substances that stabilize emulsions by reducing surface tension at the interface of the two immiscible liquids.
 
• They can be natural, like lecithin, or synthetic, like polysorbates.
 
 
 
• **Colloid**
 
 
• A colloid is a mixture where one substance is dispersed evenly throughout another at a microscopic level.
 
• Examples include gels, foams, sols, and emulsions.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Emulsions**
 
 
• Emulsions are typically opaque or translucent.
 
• They can be broken down by heating, freezing, or adding an electrolyte.
